### Country-specific policy context

<div class="country-policy-context">A few important additional points about P. vivax case management in Somalia help complete the picture:<br><br>1) Mixed approach for treatment<br>All uncomplicated malaria cases are generally treated as ACT-treated malaria (Artemether�lumefantrine) regardless of species in most settings<br>This simplifies case management where microscopy/speciation is limited<br><br>2) Relapse is a key challenge<br>Plasmodium vivax malaria can relapse from dormant liver stages (hypnozoites)<br>This means:<br>Treating only blood stages is not enough<br>Radical cure is essential but often inconsistently applied.<br><br>3) Limited radical cure implementation<br>Use of Primaquine is recommended for radical cure<br>However:<br>G6PD testing is not widely available<br>Therefore radical cure is incomplete or inconsistently given in practice.<br><br>4) Diagnosis limitations affect management<br>Many facilities rely on rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs)<br>RDTs often:<br>Do not clearly differentiate P. vivax from P. falciparum<br>This leads to uniform treatment with ACTs.<br><br>5) Follow-up and adherence gaps<br>Follow-up visits (especially Day 3 and Day 14) are often:<br>Not consistently done<br>This makes it harder to:<br>Confirm cure<br>Detect relapse or treatment failure early.<br><br>6) Overall program priority<br>National focus is mainly on:<br>Reducing overall malaria burden<br>Strengthening case management<br>P. vivax is increasingly recognized but still less prioritized than falciparum in practice</div>
